arxiv-2203-14996.title: Comparing in context: Improving cosine similarity measures with a metric tensor
arxiv-2203-14996.creator: Isa M. Apallius de Vos, Adriana D. Correia
arxiv-2203-14996.description: Abstract Cosine similarity is a widely used measure of the relatedness of pre-trained word embeddings, trained on a language modeling goal. Datasets such as WordSim-353 and SimLex-999 rate how similar words are according to human annotators, and as such are often used to evaluate the performance of language models.

arxiv-2205-14132.title: The gap between a variational problem and its occupation measure relaxation
arxiv-2205-14132.creator: Milan Korda, Rodolfo Ríos-Zertuche
arxiv-2205-14132.description: Abstract Recent works have proposed linear programming relaxations of variational optimization problems subject to nonlinear PDE constraints based on the occupation measure formalism. The main appeal of these methods is the fact that they rely on convex optimization, typically semidefinite programming. In this work we close an open question related to this approach.

arxiv-2310-17013.title: Whitepaper on Reusable Hybrid and Multi-Cloud Analytics Service Framework Conference: White paper produced by the NIST Public Working Group on Big Data; White paper produced by the NIST Public Working Group on Big Data; Washington, D.C. NIST Public Working Group on Big Data, Washington, D.C. CCS: In
arxiv-2310-17013.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Over the last several years, the computation landscape for conducting data analytics has completely changed. While in the past, a lot of the activities have been undertaken in isolation by companies, and research institutions, today’s infrastructure constitutes a wealth of services offered by a variety of providers that offer opportunities for reuse, and interactions while leveraging service collaboration, and service cooperation. This document focuses on expanding analytics services to develop a framework for reusable hybrid multi-service data analytics.

arxiv-2402-04239.title: CAST: Clustering self-Attention using Surrogate Tokens for efficient transformers
arxiv-2402-04239.creator: Adjorn van Engelenhoven, Nicola Strisciuglio & Estefanía Talavera
arxiv-2402-04239.description: Abstract The Transformer architecture has shown to be a powerful tool for a wide range of tasks. It is based on the self-attention mechanism, which is an inherently computationally expensive operation with quadratic computational complexity: memory usage and compute time increase quadratically with the length of the input sequences, thus limiting the application of Transformers.

arxiv-2404-03805.title: Blessing of dimension in Bayesian inference on covariance matrices
arxiv-2404-03805.creator: Shounak Chattopadhyay, Anru R. Zhang, David Dunson
arxiv-2404-03805.description: Abstract Bayesian factor analysis is routinely used for dimensionality reduction in modeling of high-dimensional covariance matrices. Factor analytic decompositions express the covariance as a sum of a low rank and diagonal matrix. In practice, Gibbs sampling algorithms are typically used for posterior computation, alternating between updating the latent factors, loadings, and residual variances.

arxiv-2409-07358.title: Almost sure central limit theorems for parabolic/hyperbolic Anderson models with Gaussian colored noises Thanks: Panqiu Xia is partially supported by NSF grant DMS-2246850.
arxiv-2409-07358.creator: Panqiu Xia and Guangqu Zheng
arxiv-2409-07358.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Panqiu Xia and Guangqu Zheng. This short note is devoted to establishing the almost sure central limit theorem for the parabolic/hyperbolic Anderson models driven by colored-in-time Gaussian noises, completing recent results on quantitative central limit theorems for stochastic partial differential equations. We combine the second-order Gaussian Poincaré inequality with Ibragimov and Lifshits’ method of characteristic functions, effectively overcoming the challenge from the lack of Itô tools in this colored-in-time setting, and achieving results that are inaccessible with previous methods.

arxiv-2501-13291.title: Are We Learning the Right Features? A Framework for Evaluating DL-Based Software Vulnerability Detection Solutions
arxiv-2501-13291.creator: Satyaki Das, Syeda Tasnim Fabiha, Saad Shafiq, Nenad Medvidović
arxiv-2501-13291.description: Abstract Recent research has revealed that the reported results of an emerging body of deep learning-based techniques for detecting software vulnerabilities are not reproducible, either across different datasets or on unseen samples. This paper aims to provide the foundation for properly evaluating the research in this domain.

arxiv-2508-18747.title: Some optimal recovery problems for operators on classes of L L -space valued functions
arxiv-2508-18747.creator: V. Babenko, V. Kolesnyk, O. Kovalenko
arxiv-2508-18747.description: Abstract . We solve three optimal recovery problems for operators on classes of L L –space (which is a semilinear metric space with two additional axioms that connect the metric with the algebraic operations) valued functions that are defined by a majorant of their modulus of continuity.

arxiv-2605-18068.title: Improving Spatio-Temporal Residual Error Propagation by Mitigating Over-Squashing
arxiv-2605-18068.creator: Seyed Mohamad Moghadas, Esther Rodrigo Bonet, Bruno Cornelis, Adrian Munteanu

britannica-1911-cromarty-george-mackenzi.title: Cromarty, George MacKenzie, 1st Earl of (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)

pmc-10738279.title: REDUCING UNPLANNED HOSPITALIZATIONS OF NURSING HOME RESIDENTS: A PROCESS EVALUATION OF INTERCARE
pmc-10738279.creator: Franziska Zuniga, Thekla Brunkert, Kornelia Basinska, Raphaëlle-Ashley Guerbaai, Christine Serdaly, Nathalie Wellens
pmc-10738279.description: The INTERCARE study provided evidence for a complex intervention to reduce unplanned hospitalizations in 11 Swiss nursing homes. The six intervention components were strengthening of interprofessional collaboration, introduction of a nurse with in-depth geriatric training (INTERCARE nurse), comprehensive geriatric assessment, advanced care planning, evidence-based tools, and data-driven quality improvement.

pmc-10744588.title: Preparation and Characterization of Modified ZrO2/SiO2/Silicone-Modified Acrylic Emulsion Superhydrophobic Coating
pmc-10744588.creator: Jiaxin Ben, Peipei Wu, Yancheng Wang, Jie Liu, Yali Luo, Sergei A Kulinich
pmc-10744588.description: Superhydrophobic coatings have increasingly become the focal point of research due to their distinctive properties like water resistance, wear resistance, and acid-base resilience. In pursuit of maximizing their efficiency, research has primarily revolved around refining the fabrication process and the composition of emulsion/nanoparticle coatings. We innovatively devised a superhydrophobic coating by employing a spraying technique.

pmc-10833411.title: Synthesis and redetermination of the crystal structure of NbF5
pmc-10833411.creator: Martin Möbs, Florian Kraus
pmc-10833411.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). NbF5 was synthesized in high purity by direct fluorination. IR and Raman spectroscopy confirms the high purity. The crystal structure was redetermined at 100 K with higher precision. Chemical context NbF5 was first synthesized by Ruff and Schiller (Ruff, 1909 ▸; Ruff & Schiller, 1911 ▸) from the reaction of Nb metal with elemental fluorine or from the reaction of NbCl5 with anhydrous HF.

pmc-10849928.title: MMP‐2 regulates Src activation via repression of the CHK/MATK tumor suppressor in osteosarcoma
pmc-10849928.creator: Deanna V Maybee, Christopher R Cromwell, Basil P Hubbard, Mohammad A M Ali
pmc-10849928.description: BackgroundDoxorubicin, a first‐line anticancer drug for osteosarcoma treatment, has been the subject of recent research exploring the mechanisms behind its chemoresistance and its ability to enhance cell migration at sublethal concentrations. Matrix metalloproteinase‐2 (MMP‐2), a type IV collagenase and zinc‐dependent endopeptidase, is well‐known for degrading the extracellular matrix and promoting cancer metastasis.

pmc-11339329.title: The perceived beauty of art is not strongly calibrated to the statistical regularities of real-world scenes
pmc-11339329.creator: Alexander Swartz, Alice E. Skelton, George Mather, Jenny M. Bosten, John Maule, Anna Franklin
pmc-11339329.description: Aesthetic judgements are partly predicted by image statistics, although the extent to which they are calibrated to the statistics of real-world scenes and the ‘visual diet’ of daily life is unclear. Here, we investigated the extent to which the beauty ratings of Western oil paintings from the JenAesthetics dataset can be accounted for by real-world scene statistics.

pmc-11402047.title: Developmental variations of the reproductive organs of ganders from different goose breeds and the underlying mechanisms
pmc-11402047.creator: Haoyu Yan, Jiasen Chen, Enhua Qing, Xiaopeng Li, Wanxia Wang, Zihan Ling, Zhengyang Chen, Shuhan Jiang, Yue Yan, Shilin Deng, Jiwei Hu, Liang Li, Jiwen Wang, Shenqiang Hu
pmc-11402047.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A deep understanding of the dynamics and mechanisms of male reproductive tract development is necessary for adoption of either genetic techniques or environmental management practices for improving fertility and hatchability in poultry. However, compared with other poultry such as chickens and ducks, less is known about the age- and breed-related changes in the reproductive tract development of domestic goose ganders exhibiting relatively poor reproductive performance as well as the regulatory mechanisms.

pmc-11478705.title: Effect of Personalized Prebiotic and Probiotic Supplements on the Symptoms of Irritable Bowel Syndrome: An Open-Label, Single-Arm, Multicenter Clinical Trial
pmc-11478705.creator: Nozomi Matsuura, Masaya Kanayama, Yuta Watanabe, Hirokazu Yamada, Loukia Lili, Akira Torii
pmc-11478705.description: Background/Objectives: Prebiotics and probiotics have been reported to improve symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Nevertheless, the effects of prebiotics/probiotics can vary depending on the IBS subtypes. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of personalized prebiotic and probiotic supplements based on intestinal microbiota and IBS subtypes in patients.

pmc-11610936.title: DNA-directed termination of mammalian RNA polymerase II
pmc-11610936.creator: Lee Davidson, Jérôme O Rouvière, Rui Sousa-Luís, Takayuki Nojima, Nicholas J Proudfoot, Torben Heick Jensen, Steven West
pmc-11610936.description: In this study, Davidson et al. report that mammalian RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) can terminate transcription directly at T-tracts, independent of the mechanisms that drive polyadenylation site-directed termination by RNAPII. This DNA-directed reduction in RNAPII-driven transcription, occurring at snRNAs and promoter-proximal regions, highlights an alternative global but conserved mechanism for transcription regulation by RNAPII.

pmc-11663879.title: Emerging influence of RNA post-transcriptional modifications in the synovial homeostasis of rheumatoid arthritis
pmc-11663879.creator: Madiha Fatima, Fengmei Huang, Xiaohong Fu
pmc-11663879.description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an important autoimmune disease that affects synovial tissues, accompanied by redness, pain, and swelling as main symptoms, which will limit the quality of daily life and even cause disability. Multiple coupling effects among the various cells in the synovial micro-environment modulate the poor progression and development of diseases.

pmc-12515788.title: Interrupting prolonged sitting reduces postprandial GIP but not GLP‐1 responses in type 2 diabetes
pmc-12515788.creator: Beth K Logan, Robyn Larsen, Julian W Sacre, Neale D Cohen, Gavin W Lambert, Michael J Wheeler, Neville Owen, Bronwyn A Kingwell, David W Dunstan, Paddy C Dempsey
pmc-12515788.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Postprandial GLP‐1 and GIP potentiate insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells. 1 In type 2 diabetes (T2D), although the insulinotropic effect of GLP‐1 is preserved, GIP exhibits aberrant signalling at beta cells, attenuating insulin secretion. 1 Breaking up prolonged sitting with brief bouts of activity can improve postprandial glucose, insulin, lipids, and blood pressure responses in T2D 2 , 3 , 4 ; however, the effect of these behaviours on incretin hormone responses in T2D remains unknown.

pmc-12552891.title: Successful Treatment of Refractory IgA‐Mediated Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia With Bortezomib
pmc-12552891.creator: Silvia Neri, Corien L. Eckhardt, Boukje M. Beuger, Folman Folman, Eva Rettenbacher, Hanke L. Matlung, Taco W. Kuijpers, Josephine M. I. Vos, Robin van Bruggen
pmc-12552891.description: IntroductionIgA‐mediated autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is a rare condition associated with severe hemolysis and limited therapeutic response. Bortezomib, a proteasome inhibitor, targets plasma cells responsible for autoantibody production. Here, we describe a case of refractory IgA‐mediated AIHA in a 13‐year‐old boy presenting with severe hemolysis, who was successfully treated with bortezomib.

pmc-12656199.title: Evaluation of Copper-Induced Cytotoxicity and Transcriptomic Change Using a RTgill-W1 Cell Line as an Alternative Replacing Fish Test
pmc-12656199.creator: Jin Wuk Lee, Ilseob Shim, Kyunghwa Park, Desheng Pei, Panpan Jia
pmc-12656199.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The RTgill-W1 cell line serves as an alternative for acute fish toxicity testing. This study aims to study the reliability of the RTgill-W1 cell line in copper cytotoxicity using transcriptomic analysis followed by comparison with existing literature. As a result, the study found that the average EC50 (375 μg/L ± 181 μg/L) in cell viability was similar to previous literature results (0.093–530 μg/L), suggesting the system’s reliability as an alternative.

pmc-12983192.title: Spatial Distance and Temporal Attentional Focus Modulate Voluntary Action Preparation and Awareness
pmc-12983192.creator: Gaiqing Kong, Bastien Barlerin, Clément Desoche, Luke Miller, Francesco Pavani, Alessandro Farnè, Marine Vernet
pmc-12983192.description: Peripersonal space (PPS)—the immediate space surrounding the body—modulates perception and motor control. However, its impact on how voluntary actions are initiated and subjectively experienced remains underexplored. Similarly, how directing attention to different phases of an action, such as intention formation versus execution, and anticipating outcomes of an action, modulates the neural readiness for movement, has yet to be fully examined.

pmc-13141788.title: A porous andesite-stabilized nZVI (CMC) composite for efficiently removing Cd(II) and Pb(II) from electroplating wastewater
pmc-13141788.creator: Zheng Wang
pmc-13141788.description: SummaryThe treatment of electroplating wastewater containing toxic Pb(II) and Cd(II) requires efficient adsorbents. To address the agglomeration and oxidation of nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI), we developed a novel composite, AM-nZVI-CMC, by stabilizing nZVI with carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) on a porous acid-modified andesite matrix (AM). Characterization confirmed uniform dispersion of nZVI particles (23–72 nm).

pmc-13373426.title: Proximal and Distal Femoral Fracture. A Longitudinal Retrospective Survival Analysis
pmc-13373426.creator: David Briz, Carmen da Casa, José M de Haro, Carmen Pablos, Alfonso González-Ramírez, Juan F Blanco
pmc-13373426.description: BackgroundOsteoporotic fractures represent a major public health problem, particularly in older adults. Distal femur fractures, although less frequent, have also been associated with substantial mortality, with rates approaching those of hip fractures. However, direct comparisons between both entities remain limited and heterogeneous, and it is unclear whether distal femur fractures carry a comparable prognostic burden.

pmc-13464544.title: Diffusion microstructure alterations in subcortical gray matter are associated with cognitive and motor performance in Parkinson’s disease: a pilot study
pmc-13464544.creator: Benjamin T. Newman, Ryan Foreman, Erin Donahue, Michael W. Jakowec, Andrew J. Petkus, Daniel P. Holschneider, Joseph O’Neill, Dawn M. Schiehser, Giselle Petzinger, John Darrell Van Horn

pmc-13469055.title: Mathematical study on Brinkman type carbon nanofluid flow in channel with bioconvection effect for water treatment applications
pmc-13469055.creator: Ahmad Qushairi Mohamad, Wan Nura’in Nabilah Noranuar, Mohamad Riduan Hashim, Nordin Zakaria, Sharidan Shafie, Zulkhibri Ismail, Dumitru Vieru, Anuar Jamaludin
pmc-13469055.description: Water pollution caused by the proliferation of microorganisms necessitates efficient treatment strategies to improve water quality. In this study, the bioconvective flow of a Brinkman carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-based nanofluid within a channel is analytically investigated to model water filtration processes in porous media.

pmc-13533262.title: Self‐Organized Vascularized Human Liver Spheroids: Serum‐Free Culture Conditions and Use as Tissue Building Blocks
pmc-13533262.creator: Alina Filatova, Olivera Valentirović Dann, Jennifer B. Schwarzkopf, Tengku I. Maulana, Jamina S. Gerhardus, Leon Kaysan, Katja Meier, Andreas Blaeser, Beate K. Straub, Holger Gerhardt, Ulrike A. Nuber
pmc-13533262.description: Engineering vascularized human liver tissue for in vitro and in vivo applications remains a major challenge. Here, we describe a scalable approach to generate human liver spheroids with self‐organized, lumen‐containing vascular networks and demonstrate their use as building blocks for fabricating vascularized single and multilayer tissue constructs.

pmc-13553116.title: Knowledge and smart health device use in racial-ethnic minority older adults with hypertension: a qualitative study
pmc-13553116.creator: Jany Sun, Yanjun Dong, Jimmie Boliboun, Katherine Koo, Michael Cui, Victoria M Rizzo, Jeannine M Rowe, Abby J Schwartz
pmc-13553116.description: Background and ObjectiveSmart health devices (SHDs) can improve hypertension management. Yet, SHD use among racial-ethnic minority older adults remains low, delaying potential benefits and exacerbating health disparities. Knowledge is a key determinant of SHD adoption; however, its influence on SHD use is not well understood. This study examines how knowledge affects SHD use among racial-ethnic minority older adults with hypertension.

pmc-13567708.title: Interaction of Microplastics, Plants, and Rhizosphere: A Critical Review
pmc-13567708.creator: Ying Guo, Duo Zhang, Wenxin Li, Yuntao Zhao, Wei Su, Yi Xing, Chen Hong, Jianchao Wang, Yong Cui, Han Zhang, Jiayu Chen, Bo Jiang
pmc-13567708.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Over the past decade, microplastic pollution has emerged as a subject of considerable interest and extensive research, with implications for human health and ecosystems. This paper briefly summarized the sources of microplastics and their distribution in the soil. It comprehensively addressed the effects of microplastics on the soil–plant system, including the impacts on soil physicochemical properties and plant rhizosphere microbial communities. The effects of microplastics on plant growth, along with their transformation and accumulation within plants, were evaluated.

pmc-13614365.title: Early-Stage Predominance in Breast Cancer Diagnosis Among a Rural Population: Associations With Smoking Status in a 10-Year Registry-Based Cohort Study
pmc-13614365.creator: Matthew T Foley, Allyson V Goeden, Kaylin M Burton, Kyle A Burton, Sheetal Acharya
pmc-13614365.description: BackgroundRural populations face unique barriers to preventive care and cancer screening that may influence the timing and stage of breast cancer diagnosis. Although rural residence is frequently associated with delayed cancer presentation, population-based data characterizing diagnostic patterns in rural breast cancer patients, especially in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan, remain limited.
